resources.string: Each tag becomes a YouTube search here. What it finds goes to Chrome.
Each tag opens its hashtag page, then dwells on posts from it.
The signal that actually moves the feed
New tags grow much faster once the old watch history stops voting. This opens the page. The clearing is yours to click.
Instagram has no watch-history switch. What it does expose is the list of things you have liked, and that list is a live input to Explore.

Google will not let an app sign you into YouTube inside its own browser, so this app never holds your YouTube account. It searches your tags here — searching needs no login — then hands the videos to Chrome as one playlist. Chrome is already signed in as you, so the watching counts on your real account.
Sign in below, add a few tags, then run.
Add a few tags, then build the queue.
Keep Reseed on screen while it runs — Android pauses the page behind other apps.
